To configure firewalld, you can use the `firewall-cmd` command-line tool. For example, to add a service such as `cockpit` to the firewall and make it permanent, use the following commands:

```bash
[root@host ~]# firewall-cmd --add-service=cockpit --permanent
success
[root@host ~]# firewall-cmd --reload
success
```

These commands add the `cockpit` service to the firewall rules and reload the firewall to apply the changes (Page 502). 

For more information on managing firewall rules and network interfaces via a graphical interface, refer to Page 510, which describes using the Networking button in the web console to manage firewall settings.
